newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-IRABU HAS FIRST POOR OUTING IN MINORS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-IRABU HAS FIRST POOR OUTING IN MINORS.

text.p: Japanese pitcher Hideki Irabu, making his fourth minor-league start and hoping to join the New York Yankees just after the All-Star Game, was hit hard Wednesday in a Double-A contest for the Norwich Navigators in the Eastern League.
Irabu, who had been nearly unhittable in his first three starts, was tagged for five runs and nine hits in five innings. He walked none and struck out four but gave up his first homer.
The Navigators failed to rally from the five-run deficit and dropped a 7-3 decision to the Binghamton Mets.
After throwing 14 scoreless innings in his three previous outings, Irabu surrendered a run in the second and four in the fourth before being lifted to start the sixth inning.
Irabu, who signed a four-year, $12.8 million contract with the New York Yankees in late May, was making his second start at Double-A after two starts at Class-A Tampa.
The hard-throwing right-hander is expected to start for Triple-A Columbus before joining the Yankees sometime around the All-Star break in July.

When Irabu agreed to terms, the Yankees sent the San Diego Padres $3 million in cash, outfielder Ruben Rivera and minor-league pitcher Rafael Medina. In addition to Irabu, New York received minor-leaguers Homer Bush, Gordon Amerson and Vernon Maxwell.
The Padres owned the rights to the 28-year-old Irabu as a result of their working agreement with the pitcher's Japanese team, the Chiba Lotte Marines.
Irabu was steadfast in his desire to pitch only for the Yankees and said was prepared to sit out the entire season if he was not traded to New York.
He was 12-6 and led the Japanese Pacific League with a 2.40 ERA last season.

Irabu would become the fourth Japanese player in the major leagues, joining three other pitchers -- Hideo Nomo of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shigetoshi Hasegawa of the Anaheim Angels and Takashi Kashiwada of the New York Mets.
